thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: High error rate detected in streaming-proxy (eu-central). 5xx spike + streaming disconnects. error_rate_5xx=7.8% over 3m, conn-resets up 4x. paging alert also firing. Auto-pager: oncall=chris. thread_ts=1978888888

chris: I'm on it. quick snapshot: spike coincides with a traffic burst from a few large tenants; gateway logs show 'client canceled stream' and 'upstream sent last frame then closed' with chunked encoding partials.

ops-bot: Recent infra events: LB scale-up at 1978888600, proxy-config v12 applied at 1978888700 (keepalive/tcp-timeout changes). No deploys in runtime.

santiago: can we triage impact? which customers affected and fallback state?

cs-bot: Notified CS. Two enterprise customers reported truncated live transcripts and occasional 502s. They are in eu-central.

emily: mitigation ideas: 1) revert proxy-config v12 2) enforce per-connection max chunks to avoid head-of-line 3) enable immediate paged fallback for new streams >1.5s 4) route heavy tenants to dedicated pool. Recommend quick revert + paged fallback.

chris: agree. start with non-invasive: enable paged fallback and bump read-timeout to tolerate chunked writes, then if still bad revert. Who can flip fallback?

emily: running:
```
featurectl set streaming.paginate_on_slow --region=eu-central --threshold=1500ms --duration=15m
```
Applied.

deploy-bot: config-change accepted (cfg-1978888896), expected propagation 30s.

chris: increasing proxy read timeout to 90s (was 30s) to reduce premature upstream closes: `proxyctl set --region=eu-central read_timeout=90s`

ops-bot: read_timeout change applied. LB drain checks will apply momentarily.

santiago: checking logs for OOMs or runtime restarts. runtime metric: memory spikes noted on runtime-3 around 1978888890 with GC thrash but not OOM. KV-cache error counters spiked too.

emily: that suggests backend slowdowns causing upstream to close mid-chunk. If read_timeout helps, great. If not, we should isolate the tenant.

chris: isolating two heavy tenantIDs: tenant-omega and tenant-phi. Routing them to dedicated-pool: `rtrctl move --tenant=tenant-omega,tenant-phi --to=dedicated-eu`

deploy-bot: routing change queued id=rt-1978888908, expected converge at 1978888925.

ops-bot: metrics 2m after mitigations: 5xx down from 7.8% -> 2.0%, conn-resets down 65%. Streaming latency P95 improved.

cs-bot: informing customers: temporary fallback to paged responses and retries enabled; minimal feature impact expected.

emily: capturing a raw proxy trace of a failing session for RCA. log snippet:
```
[1978888902] client 10.20.30.40 stream-id=xyz chunked: received [512B] expected [1024B]
[1978888903] upstream 10.3.4.5 closed connection: reason=write_error
[1978888904] proxy sent 502 to client; client reset stream
```
Backend thread dump shows thread blocked on remote KV lookup for ~800ms.

chris: picture: backend latency caused partial chunk flush then close -> proxy interpreted as upstream close -> client sees truncated stream. Permanent fixes: tune KV cache, increase backend concurrency, add tenant isolation circuit-breaker.

santiago: opened incident ticket INC-2026-4321 for RCA and capacity changes. Assigning to eng-runtime for KV improvements and eng-platform for routing automation.

chris: for now mark mitigated. We'll keep paged fallback for 2 hours and monitor. Emily, follow up on backend retries and GC tuning.

emily: will do. also suggest adding an observability trace that correlates chunk-boundary closes with backend latency for easier detection.

cs-bot: sent customer notes. Next update at +60m or on resolution.

chris: handing to oncall morning SRE (santiago) for follow-up and RCA. If we see a regression re-open. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> monitoring (1978889022).
